title: Swahili Maharagwe ya Nazi
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: KEN121 is a Coastal Cuisine category entry for Maharagwe ya Nazi. The primary recipe with full heritage, regional map, and cultural notes is KEN014. Both describe the same beloved Swahili coconut bean stew.

desc: Maharagwe ya Nazi — red kidney beans slowly simmered in rich coconut milk with onions, tomatoes, garlic, ginger, and warm spices. A cornerstone of Swahili coastal cuisine and one of the most satisfying vegetarian dishes in Kenya. See KEN014 for the full recipe.
longDesc: Along the Kenyan coast, where coconuts are part of everyday life, this creamy bean stew has nourished families for generations. The coconut milk transforms humble beans into something extraordinary. Served with Wali wa Nazi, it is the definitive Swahili vegetarian meal.
ingredients: 500g dried red kidney beans — soaked overnight
equipment: Large cooking pot or pressure cooker
steps: Drain soaked beans. Cook in fresh water for 60—75 minutes until completely tender. Drain, reserve 1 cup liquid.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden — 6—8 minutes.
Add garlic and ginger. Cook 1 minute.
Add tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 6—8 minutes until thick.
Add curry powder and turmeric. Stir 1 minute.
Add cooked beans and reserved liquid. Stir to coat.
Pour in coconut milk. Mix gently.
Simmer on low for 10—15 minutes — do not boil hard.
chefTips: Never boil vigorously after adding coconut milk.
Lightly mash a few beans to thicken naturally.
Fresh coconut milk gives an incomparable flavour.
commonMistakes: Boiling coconut milk hard — it splits.
cookingScience: See KEN014 for the full cooking science of this dish.
sustainabilityTips: Kidney beans are nitrogen-fixing — environmentally responsible.
reheating: Gently on stovetop with splash of coconut milk.
